fundamental.summary: MU's reported numbers are exceptional: revenue +346% YoY, an 80% operating margin and a 67% ROE with D/E of about 0.06. At 6.8x forward EPS the stock looks cheap, but the desk reads this as price-led, peak-cycle memory economics, where a low forward multiple is the classic cyclical trap. Earnings quality fails the test: trailing FCF of $7.6B is only about 15% of roughly $50B TTM net income (0.6% FCF yield, about 160x P/FCF), so the valuation depends entirely on forward earnings turning into cash. The desk is modestly positive on the EPS cushion and the clean balance sheet, but below consensus on the multiple: we do not underwrite the re-rate to about 9.5x forward that the $1,516 Street target implies.
key_points: EPS cushion: forward EPS of $159.49 is 3.6x trailing $44.27. At 6.8x forward (a 14.7% earnings yield), even a 50% cut to consensus leaves the stock at about 13.6x, so the price already assumes a large fade.

DuPont: ROE of 66.6% = 55.9% net margin x only about 1.19 combined turnover and leverage, with D/E about 0.06. Returns are margin-driven and high quality. There is no refinancing or covenant risk, and the balance sheet can fund capex through a downturn.

Revenue decomposition (inference): revenue up about 4.5x YoY alongside an 80% operating margin can only be mostly price/mix (ASP), not volume. That is the part of memory earnings most likely to fall back.

Cash conversion decides the case: at the trailing ~15% FCF/NI rate, the 14.7% forward earnings yield is only about 2.2% in FCF. Capitalizing trailing FCF at 3% growth would need a WACC-g spread of about 0.6% (WACC about 3.6%) to justify $1.22T.

Variant view: the Street is near-unanimous (46 analysts, 1.37 mean rating, $1,515.54 target = +40%, about 9.5x forward). We are BELOW consensus on the multiple: upside is limited to EPS delivery until durability and cash conversion are proven.

Catalyst and kill criteria: the 9/30 AMC print and guide, 3 days out. Upgrade if FCF conversion moves toward net income with margins holding. Turn negative if guided margins roll over from the ~80% operating level, or if capex steps up without matching pricing.
risks: Low-P/E cyclical trap: P/B of 12.1x and trailing P/S of 13.5x are extreme for a memory maker. If pricing normalizes, EPS and the multiple fall together.
The moat is an efficient-scale oligopoly, not pricing power. Industry supply discipline sets margins, which caps conviction and shortens any terminal value.

Accrual/capex gap: about $50B of TTM earnings produced only $7.6B of FCF. If capex or working capital keeps absorbing earnings, the cheap forward P/E is not real, and industry capex surges are what have historically ended memory up-cycles.
The growth figures are base effects: EPS +1,369% and a PEG of 0.16 come off a low year-ago base and say nothing about sustainable growth.
Binary event in 3 days after a +15.3% one-month run: the guide, not the beat, will set the reaction.
The market is not paying for the forward numbers: the stock is 4.4% below its level of 3 months ago while forward EPS is 3.6x trailing. That fits a market treating these earnings as temporary.

But positioning is one-sided: short interest fell about 8% during a +15% one-month run, leaving little squeeze fuel, and the 9/30 AMC print lands on PCE day, ahead of ISM Manufacturing and payrolls. Street consensus: mean rating 1.37 across 46 analysts (strong-buy territory) and a mean target of $1,515.54, +40% vs $1,082. Sell-side conviction is far ahead of a stock that is still -4.4% over 3 months.

Event stacking: earnings, PCE, ISM and payrolls all land within about 48 hours. A macro surprise can override the company news.
Macro headline risk from trusted sources: IBD notes 'surging yields' and 'Trump rejects Iran deal'. Growth stocks are ignoring yields for now, and that can reverse quickly.
Options: long calls held through 9/30 are a pure event bet exposed to the post-print drop in implied volatility. Being right on direction can still lose money.
The bullish story hangs on one date. If the print disappoints, there is no other near-term company catalyst in the news to rebuild it.

macro.summary: The regime helps: SPY is risk-on above rising 50-day and 200-day averages, VIX is calm at 14.9, and Technology, MU's sector, is the only leading sector. The cautions are narrow leadership (Industrials, Materials, Consumer Cyclical and Financials all lag, so the broad manufacturing cycle is not confirming), rising Treasury yields, and a print that lands inside a GDP/PCE, ISM and payrolls cluster while US-China talks are pending. There is no macro veto: the regime allows normal size but not above-normal, and argues against adding before the 9/29-10/5 event window.
key_points: Risk appetite is supportive: SPY is 1.5% above its 50DMA and up 0.9% over one month, in a risk-on trend. VIX is 14.9, in the calm (<15) regime.

Sector rotation: Technology leads while both defensives (Utilities, Real Estate) and cyclicals (Industrials, Basic Materials, Consumer Cyclical, Financials) lag. This is a narrow, tech-concentrated market, and MU is riding the leadership trade.

Rate channel: D/E of about 0.06 means no refinancing exposure, and at 6.8x forward EPS the stock is not priced like a long-duration asset. MU's rate risk runs through the growth/capex cycle and a de-rating of crowded tech, not through financing costs.

Cyclical read: 6.8x forward vs 24.4x trailing is how markets price a cyclical they think is near its peak. With ISM-sensitive sectors lagging, MU's demand looks concentrated in tech/AI spending rather than a broad cyclical upswing.
Calendar: JOLTS 9/29; GDP and PCE 9/30 (print day, AMC); ISM Manufacturing and jobless claims 10/1; Nonfarm Payrolls 10/2; ISM Services 10/5.

Geopolitics (trusted MT Newswires): US-China talks are pending, with Middle East and US-Iran tensions ongoing. Semiconductors are the sector most exposed to export-control and tariff outcomes. Lower-trust reports crediting chipmakers for last week's gains and a 'bond market warning' are context only.
risks: Break scenario 1 (hawkish): hot PCE or payrolls extend the rise in yields, the crowded, lone-leading tech sector de-rates, and MU trades with the group whatever its own print says.
Break scenario 2 (growth scare): weak ISM, payrolls or GDP revive fears about cyclical demand and push memory multiples lower still.
Break scenario 3 (policy): a failed US-China round escalates export controls or tariffs, which hit semis first.
Correlation: with leadership this narrow, MU shares one driver with the rest of any tech/AI exposure. In a rotation it behaves as the same position, not a diversifier.
Complacency: VIX below 15 going into a dense event window leaves room for a sharp jump in volatility.

EPS up 272.9% against revenue up 57.7% implies latest-quarter net margin about 2.4x the year-ago level. Valuation: 32.8x trailing vs 19.3x forward ($17.17 -> $29.12 EPS, about +70%), PEG 0.66. Each 1x change in the forward P/E is worth about $29/share (about 5% of the price), so the stock is sensitive to both earnings delivery and the multiple.

fundamental.summary: Atlassian makes strong cash returns: revenue grew 27.6% on about $6.6B of TTM sales (implied by 7.2x P/S), it produced $1.66B of FCF (about a 25% margin, Rule of 40 about 53), and its debt is less than one year of FCF. GAAP earnings are negative, though (EPS -$0.21, ROE -4.5%). FCF exceeds net income by about $1.7B, which usually means large SBC addbacks, so headline FCF overstates what owners actually earn. After a +138% re-rate in three months the stock trades at about 29x FCF and 26x forward EPS that is almost certainly adjusted. A reverse DCF shows the price already assumes about 20% FCF compounding for five years, mid-range of a ~$158-226 grid, so there is no margin of safety. Every bull point we can see is already consensus (31 analysts at a 1.55 mean rating, mean target only +8.6%), so this is a quality business priced fully: HOLD-grade until the Oct 29 print proves growth can last.
key_points: Growth and cash: 27.6% revenue growth at ~$6.6B TTM scale with a ~25% FCF margin gives a Rule of 40 of ~53 on FCF (~40 on the 12.3% operating margin). Implied debt of ~$1.2B (1.16x D/E on ~$1.06B book equity) is ~0.7x annual FCF. The high D/E comes from thin book equity (P/B ~45x), not from heavy borrowing.

Earnings quality only partly checks out. The 12.3% operating margin and the -0.8% net margin leave an ~$0.86B gap below the operating line (or the two figures cover different periods) that needs explaining. FCF exceeds GAAP net income by ~$1.7B (~26% of revenue). SBC and share count are not in our data, so FCF minus SBC and dilution cannot be checked.

Multiples: 3.5% FCF yield (28.7x P/FCF), 7.2x sales, PEG 1.96, no trailing P/E. The 26x forward P/E rests on $7.22 of EPS that is almost certainly non-GAAP, since trailing GAAP EPS is -$0.21. We have no peer or historical multiples, so valuation rests on an absolute DCF only.

Reverse DCF on reported FCF (our own assumptions, 5-year explicit period): at 10% WACC and 3% terminal growth, the price needs ~20% FCF CAGR. Across 9-11% WACC and 2.5-3% terminal growth, fair value spans ~$158-226/share. The price sits mid-range, and terminal value is 74-81% of EV, at or above our 75% comfort line. A 15% CAGR gives ~$158 (-16%); a 25% CAGR gives ~$231 (+23%). All of this is before any SBC haircut or net-cash adjustment (cash is not in our data).

The re-rating did most of the work. On today's TTM figures, the move from ~$79 to $187.74 took P/FCF from ~12x to ~29x and forward P/E from ~11x to 26x. That expansion is only justified if growth is holding or speeding up, and we have no growth history, NRR or gross-margin data to confirm it.

Catalyst and triggers: Oct 29 AMC print (32 days). Upgrade if growth holds in the high-20s, FCF margin stays intact, and the price falls toward the low end of the grid. Downgrade if the print or guidance implies FCF compounding nearer 15% than 20% (fair value ~$158).
risks: Downside risk is larger than upside: a multiple that expanded ~2.4x in one quarter is exposed to any slowdown from 27.6% growth at the Oct 29 print.
SBC and dilution: if stock comp explains the FCF-GAAP gap, the true multiple on owner earnings is far above 29x FCF and the 26x forward P/E flatters the stock.
Missing and inconsistent data (operating vs net margin; no cash, gross margin, NRR, SBC, peer or history data) put wide error bars on every valuation figure.
The moat is inferred from the economics (growth plus ~25% FCF margin), not shown directly. Nothing in our data tests whether a well-funded rival could erode it.
Crowded consensus: 31 analysts at a 1.55 mean rating and reported institutional ownership of 104.8% leave few new buyers if fundamentals disappoint.

technical.summary: Price is the main evidence, and it says the trend is clearly up: above both the 50- and 200-day SMAs, +138% over 3 months and +176% over 6 months, and ~132 points ahead of SPY over 3 months. The pace has slowed sharply, though: ~+114% in the prior two months versus +11% in the latest month. RSI(14) at 48.5 shows about three weeks of stalling, so this is a pause after a steep run that has worked off overbought conditions over time. It only confirms continuation if it breaks upward. We lean long with the trend, but timing is fair at best, and 95% annualized volatility calls for wide stops based on price structure and small positions scaled to volatility.

Once short covering runs out, an important source of recent buying disappears.
Next week's major economic releases can hit high-momentum software stocks regardless of company news.

macro.summary: The macro backdrop helps rather than blocks: SPY is risk-on above rising 50- and 200-day averages, VIX is calm at 14.9, and Technology is the only leading sector, so TEAM sits in the market's favored group. But TEAM's value depends heavily on distant earnings (26x forward EPS, 7.2x sales, ~3.5% FCF yield, negative GAAP margin), and the one trusted rates headline shows Treasury yields rising. The scenario that breaks the thesis is a hot PCE (9/30) plus strong payrolls (10/2) pushing real yields up and shrinking software multiples, or money rotating out of this unusually narrow tech leadership. No veto today, but position size should stay moderate rather than full until this data week is over.
key_points: Market regime: risk-on. SPY is 1.5% above a rising 50-day average and above a rising 200-day average, up 0.9% over 1 month (a steady climb, not euphoria). VIX at 14.9 (calm) supports appetite for volatile growth stocks.

Sectors: Technology is the only leader, while defensives (Utilities, Real Estate) and cyclicals (Materials, Financials, Industrials, Consumer Cyclical) all lag. TEAM benefits, but leadership this narrow is crowded and prone to rotation. Low-trust headlines credit chipmakers for tech strength (context only), so software may be riding the sector label rather than leading it.

How macro reaches this stock: through the discount rate, not credit. At 26x forward EPS, 7.2x sales and a negative GAAP margin, the multiple is very sensitive to real yields. Meanwhile $1.66B of FCF easily covers the debt implied by 1.16x D/E, so refinancing risk is low.

Rates: a trusted MT Newswires item (9/25) shows Treasury yields rising while stocks still rose and oil fell. Stocks are absorbing higher yields for now, but rising yields directly hurt long-duration software. A low-trust 'bond market warning' headline is context only.

Busy calendar before the Oct 29 earnings: JOLTS 9/29, GDP and PCE 9/30, ISM Manufacturing 10/1, NFP 10/2, ISM Services 10/5. Labor data matters twice for TEAM: it moves yields and it shapes the outlook for corporate hiring and IT budgets.

risks: Break scenario 1 (most direct): hot PCE and strong NFP push real yields up and long-duration software re-rates lower. A stock up 138% in 3 months would likely give back more than most.
Break scenario 2: money rotates out of narrow tech leadership into the lagging cyclical or defensive sectors.
Break scenario 3: a growth scare (weak ISM or NFP) hits corporate IT budgets. In that case bad news is bad news, and lower yields don't rescue the multiple.
Shock from calm: a geopolitical or US-China setback with VIX at 14.9 would hit the most volatile recent winners hardest.

quant.summary: The 96 composite screen comes mostly from momentum (100) and revisions (88.8). That is a strong pairing, because rising estimates back up the price move. The best argument for owning it is revisions at 88.8: estimates are rising along with the price, which is sturdier momentum than price alone.

If the exact 0.0% is a data gap, 12-1 momentum can't be measured.

Regime: the benchmark is trending up (~+6% over 3 months, implied by the 132-point relative-strength gap), which suits momentum. But a maxed-out factor score is stretched and should be expected to revert, not extrapolated. RSI 48.5 shows some of the stretch has already cooled over time.

Risk math: 95% volatility means about 6% daily and 27% monthly moves at one standard deviation. At a fixed risk budget, the position gets roughly one-third the dollars of a stock with 30% volatility. The -67.5% max drawdown needs +208% to recover, which is the downside this stock has already shown.
Sizing: our edge is an estimate, so use a quarter to half of the Kelly size on a volatility-scaled base. At $47.5B, liquidity is not the limit; volatility is.
risks: Momentum crash: volatile, below-median-quality recent winners are sold first in sharp reversals, and value 42 and quality 41 offer no support.
Revisions fading: if the 88.8 revisions score drops, momentum loses its fundamental backing and becomes price alone.
Volatility clusters: at 95% volatility, normal noise will trigger tight stops, so position size, not stop distance, has to control risk.
Data quality: an exact 0.0% 12-month return looks like missing data, so any conclusion that depends on the momentum time frame carries extra uncertainty.

bull.case: Atlassian is still growing revenue 27.6% on ~$6.6B with a ~25% FCF margin ($1.66B, Rule of 40 ~53) and debt of only ~0.7x a year's FCF, and analysts keep raising numbers (revisions 88.8), so rising earnings estimates back the price move rather than a price-only squeeze. The price has barely moved since Aug 28 ($191.52, then $192.53 on Sep 18, $187.74 now) while estimates rose, so the forward multiple is shrinking without the price falling: RSI has reset to a neutral 48.5 with price above both the 50- and 200-day SMAs, which looks like a high-tight flag rather than a top. At 26x forward EPS and a ~2 PEG the price sits mid-range of the desk's own $158-226 DCF grid, and the 25%-FCF-CAGR case reaches ~$231 (+23%); fully valued is not overvalued for a Rule-of-50 franchise. If the flat 12-month return is real, the whole run is a round trip out of an AI-fear overshoot: price is back where it was a year ago with a year of ~28% growth added, so the sales multiple is lower, not higher, than twelve months ago. Technology is the only leading sector in a calm (VIX 14.9), risk-on market, and 9.65M shares (6.1% of float) are still short and could fuel a jump on a beat. The bear's SBC haircut is an inference (SBC is not in the packet), and crowding is not a sell signal while estimates are still rising into a dated Oct 29 catalyst.
strongest_points: Revisions at 88.8: estimates are rising while price stays flat, so the forward multiple is shrinking on its own.
Undisputed fundamentals: 27.6% growth, ~25% FCF margin ($1.66B), Rule of 40 ~53, debt ~0.7x annual FCF.
Constructive base: flat since Aug 28 with RSI reset to 48.5, above both the 50- and 200-day SMAs, in the market's only leading sector.
Dated catalyst: Oct 29 AMC print; the 25%-CAGR DCF case is ~$231 (+23%) and 6.1% of float is still short.
bull.what_breaks_it: An Oct 29 print or guidance implying growth sliding toward the low-20s (FCF compounding nearer 15%, fair value ~$158), or a close below ~$168 that turns the flag into a failed top.

bear.case: The re-rating already did the work: on today's TTM numbers the run from ~$79 to $187.74 took P/FCF from ~12x to ~29x and forward P/E from ~11x to 26x, so the price now assumes ~20% FCF growth a year for five years in a DCF where terminal value is 74-81% of EV. That range is mostly assumption and offers no margin of safety [K1][K2]. Every visible pillar is consensus (31 analysts at 1.55, a mean target only +8.6% away, institutions at a reported 104.8%, short interest already down 17.8%), so there are few buyers left and an in-line print sets up a sell-the-news drop; revisions at 88.8 is the bull's best card, but it is a public screen rank every holder already sees. Earnings quality is unproven: GAAP EPS is -$0.21 and ROE -4.5% while FCF exceeds net income by ~$1.7B, and until SBC is disclosed the 26x adjusted-EPS multiple has to prove itself, not the skeptic. The momentum score of 100 is a V-shaped rebound out of a -67.5% drawdown rather than 12-1 momentum, the kind most prone to crashes, and momentum has lost money in this firm's own book (-2.5pts). The bull's round-trip reading rests on a 0.0% 12-month figure that the technical and quant desks both flag as a likely data gap; if it is real, a year of trapped holders is now at breakeven and ready to sell. At 95% annualized vol an ordinary one-sigma month (~27%) reaches the $146 structural break with no change in the story, and a hot PCE/NFP week with Treasury yields already rising hits exactly this long-duration software profile.
strongest_points: Re-rated from ~12x to ~29x P/FCF in one quarter; the price assumes ~20% FCF growth a year and sits mid-grid of $158-226 with terminal value at 74-81% of EV, so there is no margin of safety [K1][K2].
Consensus saturation: 1.55 across 31 analysts, target only +8.6% away, 104.8% institutional ownership, shorts already covered -17.8%.
Earnings quality: GAAP EPS -$0.21, ROE -4.5%, a ~$1.7B FCF-over-net-income gap likely from SBC, and an unexplained ~$0.86B gap between the 12.3% operating and -0.8% net margins.
Momentum is a rebound out of a -67.5% drawdown, has lost money here (-2.5pts) and is halved by the regime rule; 95% vol puts the $146 break one ordinary month away.
The one comparable with a known outcome, a switching-cost vertical-SaaS HOLD priced at its analysts' target, lagged SPY by 12.5% over the next 20 days [P6] (n=1, anecdotal).
bear.what_breaks_it: An Oct 29 print showing growth re-accelerating above 27.6% with raised guidance and FCF margin expansion, proving the ~20% FCF-growth bar built into the price is conservative.

base.case: Most probably the stock chops between the $168 warning line and the $204 mean target into the Oct 29 print, moved more by the tech sector and the PCE/ISM/NFP data week than by company news, continuing a stall that has left the price essentially unchanged since the Aug 28 sitting ($191.52 [P4] to $187.74). Revisions at 88.8 make a solid beat the likeliest print, but with a 1.55 consensus and price within 9% of target, a beat with steady guidance is roughly priced in, so the post-print move is large (95% vol) and close to symmetric around $187.74. The bull's flag and revisions are real but both are visible strength that the regime rule halves, and the round-trip argument rests on suspect data; the bear's valuation and SBC critiques are real but nothing is deteriorating and the trend is intact, so there is no breakdown to short. Expected 21-session excess return is near zero with wide outcomes both ways. That pays neither a share position (sizing a 95%-vol name so a gap through any sane stop fits the per-name budget shrinks a pre-print position to a token) nor calls, which face a binary event on top of expensive options. The print will turn two-sided evidence into a directional read, so wait for it.
strongest_points: Price sits mid-grid of the $158-226 DCF and 8.6% below the consensus target, so there is no edge either way at $187.74.
Four prior HOLDs at 51-55 found every pillar consensus [P1][P2][P3][P4], and the price has not moved since ($191.52 on Aug 28, $192.53 on Sep 18, $187.74 now).
An earnings binary on Oct 29 on a 95%-vol name means gap-through sizing shrinks any pre-print position to a token.
Nothing is deteriorating (revisions 88.8, trend intact, sector leading), so there is no case for a SELL either.
base.what_breaks_it: A decisive resolution before the print (a close above ~$195 with revisions still rising, or below ~$168), or a print far enough from consensus to move the stock more than a monthly sigma (~27%).

verdict.debate_summary: The bull's best point, revisions at 88.8 backing a flat month with RSI reset, held up, but the bear showed every other pillar is consensus or price-derived and that revisions, as a public screen rank, cannot serve as the firm's required pillar that is not visible strength, so the base case's near-symmetric, wide-outcome path into the Oct 29 earnings binary won. Nothing is deteriorating, so there is no SELL, and nothing is differentiated or priced with a margin of safety, so there is no BUY; conviction eases from 55 to 50 because of stricter scoring, not new information, since the regime rule (six sectors lagging) halves the momentum/screen credit that supported the prior score.
verdict.thesis: Atlassian is a good business priced as one: 27.6% growth and a ~25% FCF margin ($1.66B) are undisputed, but after a re-rate from ~12x to ~29x P/FCF the price sits mid-range of a $158-226 DCF grid that is itself mostly assumption [K1][K2], with 31 analysts at 1.55 and the mean target only +8.6% away. Macro is a tailwind, not a veto (Technology leads a calm, risk-on market), but once the regime-halved momentum/screen credit is removed, no pillar names where consensus is wrong, and the firm's own record says buying exactly this profile, extended visible strength with momentum at 100, has lost money (BUY avg -3.5%, momentum -2.5pts). Missing evidence that keeps it out, recorded per firm rule: (1) an Oct 29 print confirming high-20s growth, an FCF margin of at least 25% and steady-to-raised guidance; (2) SBC and share-count data showing owner FCF supports ~29x; (3) either a post-print close above the post-Aug-28 range or a pre-print pullback toward the $158-165 low end of the grid that provides a margin of safety. HOLD at zero weight and re-examine on the print.
verdict.bear_risk: An in-line Oct 29 print, or a hot PCE/NFP week lifting real yields first, against a 1.55 consensus and 104.8% institutional ownership, unwinding a 95%-vol V-shaped rebound toward the $146-158 zone (-16% to -22%).
verdict.watch_trigger: Upgrade to BUY if EITHER (a) after the Oct 29 AMC print confirms high-20s revenue growth, an FCF margin of at least 25% and steady-to-raised guidance, the stock closes above $195 (clearing the post-Aug-28 range); OR (b) before the print, price pulls back to $165 or lower (the low end of the $158-226 DCF grid) while still holding above the 200-day SMA.
verdict.suitable_for_calls_reason: No: the only dated catalyst is the Oct 29 earnings binary 32 days out, so a 1-6 week call either expires with no catalyst or rides into post-earnings IV crush, and 95% realized vol makes premium expensive.
verdict.suitable_for_puts_reason: No: there is no breakdown to short (price above both SMAs, revisions 88.8, sector leading), and the only downside catalyst is the same earnings binary.
verdict.horizon: 5 weeks to the Oct 29 print re-check; 3-6 months for any resulting position

The cautious lean could be wrong on the bullish side. Strong forward EPS growth would make 30x trailing reasonable on forward numbers. The desk simply can't see that data, which is why conviction is only 2.

key_points: Price is above the 50-day and 200-day averages, so the main uptrend is intact. The averages' slopes and levels aren't provided, so trend strength and exact support levels can't be checked.

The return windows imply closes of about 572.6 six months ago, 705.8 three months ago, 710.6 one month ago and 744.5 now. That is +23.3%, then +0.7% over two months, then +4.8%. Momentum is picking up again after a flat stretch rather than rising steadily.

3-month relative strength vs SPY is -0.59. Price is rising in absolute terms but flat to slightly down relative to SPY, so the index isn't leading the market this quarter. That caps conviction.

Against 20.5% annualized volatility, the 6-month +30% move is about 2.1 standard deviations, a strong trend. Last month's +4.8% is about 0.8 standard deviations, so not a blow-off. risks: The breakout could fail. If the +4.8% leg fades back into 706-711, the two-month flat stretch looks like a top rather than a base.

Buying now means chasing. A stop about 5% below, at the pre-breakout level, is less than one month's normal move (about 5.9%), so ordinary noise can trigger it. Entering here has the worst short-term reward-to-risk.

The data may be wrong. A 12-month return of exactly 0.0% can't be true alongside +30% over 6 months and a -12% 2-year max drawdown, because a flat 12 months would need a drop of 23% or more between 12 and 6 months ago. The 12-month field is probably missing data stored as zero, and the drawdown figure should be treated with caution.

CORT.debate_summary: Bull and bear agree on the facts (an intact uptrend, 31.7% revenue growth, revisions at 89.1, and a forward multiple that is only reasonable if a ~9.8x EPS ramp arrives) and split only on whether to pay for that ramp before it is printed. The base case wins: the fundamental desk is neutral, the two long-leaning desks restate the same momentum driver (halved under the lagging-sector rule), the quality pillar is stripped, and the only new information since the 9/21 HOLD is a speculative headline and a one-sigma price bounce.
CORT.thesis: Keep the existing starter on its 15% trail; do not add and do not exit. CORT is a real growth story in an intact uptrend (revenue +31.7%, FCF-positive, debt-free, revisions 89.1), but every pillar of the long case is visible consensus (Buy rating, $141 target, momentum 100, screen 93.4), and the valuation (262x trailing, 26.8x forward) rests on a ~9.8x EPS ramp from five analysts that the reported record (EPS growth lagging revenue growth, 6.6% net margin) does not yet show. With upside to the target down to ~20% against a ~15-19% stop distance and a binary print 42 days out, there is no margin of safety and no variant view to pay for. Missing evidence that keeps this out of a half-clip add, recorded per firm rule: a Nov 4 print showing net margin well above 6.6% on >=30% growth with steady or raised guidance, trusted or primary confirmation of the EU approval restated as an estimate raise, or any non-visible pillar showing where consensus is wrong.
CORT.bear_risk: The $4.40 forward EPS (9.8x trailing, five analysts) proves too high at the Nov 4 intraday print, turning 26.8x forward into ~38x or more on a 67.6%-vol name up 250% in six months, and the resulting momentum unwind gaps straight through the trail stop.
CORT.what_changed: Nothing material: the +6.8% since the 9/21 HOLD ($110.29 -> $117.78, about a one-sigma two-day move) came on a speculative-only CHMP headline that cannot move conviction, fundamentals are unchanged, and the bounce cut paper upside to the $141 target from ~28% to ~20%; the pullback holding above both averages nudges timing (conviction 46 -> 50), not the rating.

CORT.suitable_for_calls_reason: HOLD with no verified dated catalyst before the Nov 4 binary; the long case is a slow verification, not a timed 1-6 week move.
CORT.suitable_for_puts_reason: Trend intact above both averages with revisions at 89.1; no breakdown and no short thesis.

PSX.suitable_for_puts_reason: No breakdown to short: the trend is intact above the 50-day and 200-day averages with no named fundamental break, and the downside depends on an undated diplomacy outcome plus the earnings report, which makes it a bet on volatility rather than on direction.
PSX.horizon: 1-2 months (settled at the Oct 28 Q3 report)

PEB.suitable_for_puts_reason: No breakdown to short: price above the 200-DMA with the gain held and revisions rising (77.8), and a 22% short float into the 10/29 binary makes puts a squeeze-exposed coin flip.
